adventure.title: Sunrise at the Grand Palace complex
adventure.description: Getting to the Grand Palace at 7am means being the first through the gates, before the heat and the tour buses — the gilt spires in early light are something entirely different.
adventure.bonus: Be at the gate before it opens. Watch it unlock.

adventure.title: White-water kayak on the Mae Klong River (day trip)
adventure.description: Two hours west of Bangkok, the Mae Klong has class II–III rapids accessible for half-day guided kayak trips — the train market at the put-in point is a bonus.
adventure.bonus: Paddle the most difficult line through each rapid. Don't take the safe route.

adventure.title: Bouldering at Bloc+ Bangkok, Sathorn
adventure.description: Bangkok has a growing climbing gym scene in the old city area — the heat makes bouldering demanding in a different way, and the gyms stay open late.
adventure.bonus: Climb until you can't grip. Then do one more.

adventure.title: Koh Kret island bicycle escape
adventure.description: An island in the Chao Phraya north of Bangkok with no cars, Mon pottery villages, and a 7km loop — take the ferry and cycle until you've seen every corner.
adventure.bonus: Buy a clay pot from a Mon potter before you leave.

adventure.title: Night Market Motorcycle Taxi Blitz in Chatuchak
adventure.description: Hire a motorcycle taxi driver for a 30-minute rip through the gridlocked streets around Chatuchak and feel Bangkok's actual pulse.
adventure.bonus: Tell the driver 'farang price' — then negotiate in Thai numbers only using your phone calculator.

adventure.title: Climb the Prangs of Wat Arun at Dusk
adventure.description: Scaling the steep ceramic-encrusted spires of the Temple of Dawn as the sun drops over the Chao Phraya is a genuinely vertiginous Bangkok moment.
adventure.bonus: Climb to the highest accessible level and stay until the temple lights flick on — don't leave early.

adventure.title: Muay Thai Night at Rajadamnern Stadium
adventure.description: The oldest boxing stadium in Bangkok delivers raw, ritual Muay Thai where the crowd noise and ringside gamblers are half the spectacle.
adventure.bonus: Learn the Thai hand-signal betting system from the man next to you and place at least one bet.

adventure.title: Long-tail Boat Through Thonburi Canals
adventure.description: A deafening, spray-soaked ride through Bangkok's forgotten backwater villages reveals a city that still lives on the water.
adventure.bonus: Ask the driver to kill the engine for 60 seconds and sit in the silence of the klong.

social.title: Rooftop at Above Eleven, Fraser Suites Sukhumvit
social.description: Bangkok rooftops at sunset — Vertigo at Banyan Tree, Sky Bar at Lebua, or dozens of smaller options — the skyline here is genuinely dramatic in the orange light.
social.bonus: Stay for the first lights of the city coming on. That's the real view.

social.title: Muay Thai fight night at Lumpinee Stadium
social.description: Lumpinee is the most storied Muay Thai venue in the world — ringside seats are cheap by international standards and the crowd, the ritual, and the skill level are the real thing.
social.bonus: Bet on one fight — ₹100 with a stranger. Watch it differently after.

social.title: Cocktails at Teens of Thailand, Chinatown
social.description: Bangkok has a small but serious speakeasy scene in the Sukhumvit sois — a good one has no sign, great ice, and a bartender who's thought about every glass.
social.bonus: Let the bartender make you something off-menu. Tell them your last favorite drink.

social.title: Thai cooking class at Baipai Thai Cooking School
social.description: Bangkok cooking classes start at a wet market, buy ingredients directly from vendors, then cook five dishes from scratch — the market portion is better than the cooking.
social.bonus: Ask the vendor what each ingredient smells like. Then smell it.

social.title: Sunday Brunch at Talat Noi Community Market
social.description: The atmospheric Talat Noi riverside quarter hosts a loose Sunday gathering of street food, local artists, and old Chinese shophouse life that feels nothing like tourist Bangkok.
social.bonus: Find the 200-year-old Talat Noi Shrine tucked in a back alley and photograph it without using it as the main subject.

social.title: Late-Night Drinks at Maggie Choo's, Silom
social.description: A subterranean 1930s Shanghai-themed speakeasy under the Novotel where live jazz, stunning décor, and a mixed Bangkok crowd make for a genuinely glamorous night.
social.bonus: Sit at the bar, order whatever the bartender is personally proud of, and stay for two sets of live music.

social.title: Saturday at Chatuchak Weekend Market
social.description: The world's largest weekend market across 35 acres and 15,000 stalls rewards slow wanderers who get lost in the vintage, ceramic, and plant sections far from the entrance.
social.bonus: Find section 2 or 3 (antiques/vintage), pick one object with a story, and bargain in Thai using only numbers on your phone.

social.title: Friday Night at Teen Tae Bar, Ari Neighborhood
social.description: Ari's laid-back local bar strip draws Bangkok's creative class for cheap Singha, sticky bar snacks, and conversations that run past midnight.
social.bonus: Buy a round for the table nearest you and ask them to recommend somewhere to go next.

social.title: Asiatique Riverfront Night Market
social.description: A converted 1900s French-colonial warehouse on the Chao Phraya that transforms after dark into Bangkok's best open-air night market — riverside tables, a Ferris wheel, live theater, and a thousand stalls.
social.bonus: Ride the Ferris wheel. It sounds like a tourist trap. It isn't.

chill.title: Morning alms-giving at Wat Yannawa, Silom
chill.description: At 6am, monks walk their alms routes through Bangkok's old neighbourhoods — buy prepared rice and offerings from a vendor, and give respectfully, quietly, without a camera out.

chill.title: Golden hour longtail boat ride through the khlongs
chill.description: Charter a longtail for 90 minutes at golden hour to navigate Bangkok's canal network behind the Grand Palace — wooden houses, spirit houses, monks, and a city the tourists don't see.
chill.bonus: Ask the driver to go somewhere they actually like. Not the tour route.

chill.title: Meditation session in the Wat Pho gardens
chill.description: Wat Pho is the temple that codified traditional Thai massage and still runs a meditation program in its garden courts — sit for an hour in a space that has been still since the 18th century.
chill.bonus: Sit for the full session without your phone. No exceptions.

chill.title: Afternoon at Phra Athit Road riverside cafés
chill.description: Bangkok's klhong-side cafés in Phra Nakhon and Thonburi offer hammocks over the water, slow WiFi, and the kind of afternoon that makes you miss your flight.
chill.bonus: Don't set an alarm. See how long you actually stay.

chill.title: Cold brew at Roots Coffee Roasters, Ari
chill.description: Bangkok's specialty coffee scene has quietly become one of Asia's best — find a garden café in the Silom green belt, order cold brew, and stay until the evening air cools.
chill.bonus: Leave your phone in your bag the whole time. Watch the garden instead.

chill.title: Temple hop by riverboat: Wat Pho, Wat Arun, Wat Phra Kaew
chill.description: The three great temples of old Bangkok are connected by the Chao Phraya river express — a half-day circuit by boat sees the reclining Buddha, the demon guardian towers, and the Emerald Buddha.
chill.bonus: Enter all three before noon. Leave before the heat builds.

chill.title: Night Drinks on the Terrace at Sala Rattanakosin
chill.description: A rooftop bar directly across the Chao Phraya from Wat Arun where the illuminated prangs fill your entire field of vision while you drink.
chill.bonus: Arrive exactly at sunset and don't check your phone until the temple lights come on.

chill.title: Reading Afternoon at the BACC Rooftop Café
chill.description: The Bangkok Arts and Culture Centre's top-floor café sits above the Pathumwan intersection madness with wide views and zero hustle.
chill.bonus: Spend 20 minutes in the gallery on the way up — pick one piece and write one sentence about why it works.

chill.title: Sunset at Wat Pho's Garden Courtyard
chill.description: After the tourist crowds drain out, Wat Pho's shaded inner courtyards become one of the most peaceful squares of real estate in Bangkok.
chill.bonus: Book a 30-minute traditional Thai massage inside the temple — it's the original school.

chill.title: Morning Coffee at Lan Fang Yuan, Chinatown
chill.description: A marble-topped old-school coffee shop where decades-old ceiling fans, kopi served in ceramic cups, and no Wi-Fi make time genuinely slow down.
chill.bonus: Leave your phone in your pocket for the entire visit and strike up a conversation with another table.

chill.title: Afternoon at Jim Thompson House
chill.description: The teak compound of an American silk entrepreneur who vanished in the Malaysian jungle in 1967 — six traditional Thai structures with a world-class art collection and a canal garden that stops time.
chill.bonus: Find the painting the docent didn't mention in the tour. Ask about it.

chill.title: Sunset Drinks at Octave Rooftop Lounge
chill.description: A three-level rooftop bar on floors 45–49 of the Marriott Sukhumvit offers a 360-degree panorama of Bangkok's grid as it goes orange, then purple, then neon — no reservations required, arrive before 6pm.
chill.bonus: Order a drink with kaffir lime or lemongrass. Pick the cocktail with the most Thai ingredients on the menu.

chill.title: Bangkok Art and Culture Centre
chill.description: Seven floors of rotating contemporary Thai art at the Siam BTS intersection — free entry, world-class work, and a bookshop in the basement that's better than most galleries.
chill.bonus: Find one piece you genuinely don't understand. Spend five full minutes in front of it before moving on.

chill.title: Thai Massage at Wat Pho School
chill.description: The oldest and most respected massage school in Thailand operates right next to the temple — 60 minutes of traditional northern-style Thai massage by certified students, for less than the cost of lunch back home.
chill.bonus: Don't wince. Breathe through it. Ask for deeper pressure at least once.

foodie.title: Boat noodles at Guay Tiew Reua Siam, Ari
foodie.description: Boat noodles are a tiny bowl of pork blood broth with thin noodles and crispy pork — you order ten of them because they're the size of a cup and eat them at a canal-side table.
foodie.bonus: Order at least 8 bowls. That's the correct amount.

foodie.title: Tasting menu at R-Haan, Din Daeng
foodie.description: Bangkok's high-end Thai cooking scene — R-Haan, Sorn, Paste — is among the most serious in Asia; find a reservation and understand what Thai ingredients become when treated as fine dining.
foodie.bonus: Ask the chef what dish they're most proud of this season.

foodie.title: Late-night noodles at Jeh O Chula, Hua Lamphong
foodie.description: Bangkok's 24-hour noodle shophouses peak between midnight and 3am — find one in Silom with fluorescent lights and plastic stools and let it save your evening.
foodie.bonus: Go after midnight. The kitchen is better when the chef's been awake for hours.

foodie.title: Som tam at Somtum Der, Saladaeng
foodie.description: The northeastern Thai food of Isan — green papaya salad and minced meat salad with fish sauce and toasted rice — is Bangkok's most honest and punishing food.
foodie.bonus: Order both spicy. No modifications. Trust the kitchen.

foodie.title: Floating market feast at Damnoen Saduak
foodie.description: Boat vendors selling pad see ew, mango sticky rice, and grilled corn from narrow canals — touristy, yes, but the food itself is genuinely excellent.
foodie.bonus: Eat five different things from five different boats. No repeats.

foodie.title: Khao man gai at Kuang Heng, Pratunam
foodie.description: Poached chicken over rice with ginger sauce and a bowl of broth — Bangkok's best breakfast is also its cheapest and most forgiving morning-after meal.
foodie.bonus: Order the dark sauce version. It's what the locals ask for.

foodie.title: Sundowners at Vertigo and Moon Bar, Banyan Tree Bangkok
foodie.description: Bangkok's rooftop bar scene ranges from tourist traps to genuinely excellent cocktail programs — find one in Silom with a serious menu and let sunset do the design work.
foodie.bonus: Order the tasting menu of oysters. Rank them east to west by ocean.

foodie.title: Mango Sticky Rice at Kor Panich on Tanao Road
foodie.description: This 80-year-old shop on Tanao Road has been perfecting glutinous rice, fresh mango, and coconut cream since 1932 — and it still has a line.
foodie.bonus: Order a second portion immediately and eat it standing on the street.

foodie.title: Lunch at Jay Fai's Wok Kitchen on Mahachai Road
foodie.description: Bangkok's most famous street cook — goggles on, two woks blazing — serves crab omelettes and drunken noodles worth every baht of the queue.
foodie.bonus: Show up at opening, watch Jay Fai cook your dish start to finish, and tell her it's the best thing you've eaten in Asia.

foodie.title: Pre-Dawn Dim Sum at Chinatown's Yaowarat Road
foodie.description: Yaowarat's all-night dim sum carts and shark fin soup shops hit their stride after midnight when the street food vendors pack up and the serious eaters arrive.
foodie.bonus: Order something off-menu by pointing at what the table next to you is eating.

foodie.title: Street Pad Thai at Thip Samai
foodie.description: Bangkok's most famous pad thai kitchen wraps each plate in a paper-thin egg crepe — the line on Maha Chai Road moves fast and the result is worth every minute of the wait.
foodie.bonus: Order the pad thai wrapped in egg crepe and eat it standing at the street counter without utensils.

foodie.title: Boat Noodles at Wang Lang Market
foodie.description: Cross to the Wang Lang side of the Chao Phraya on the express ferry for 5 baht and step into a riverside market that serves deep pork broth noodles the size of your fist for 15 baht a bowl.
foodie.bonus: Order five small bowls instead of one large — that's how locals eat them.

foodie.title: Chef's Table at Le Normandie, Mandarin Oriental
foodie.description: Bangkok's oldest fine-dining institution occupies a riverfront room at the Mandarin Oriental where the classical French menu has been evolving since 1958 — white gloves, a Michelin star, and a Chao Phraya view at the end of a meal that doesn't hurry.
foodie.bonus: Order the cheese course. Always order the cheese course.

active.title: Morning run along the Chao Phraya riverside promenade
active.description: The river promenade from Saphan Taksin to Phra Arthit is 6km of riverside path, ferries, temples, and morning monks — run it before the heat arrives after 8am.
active.bonus: Start in the dark. Finish in the light. The river changes completely.

active.title: Wakeboard at Cable Ski Wake Board, Ramindra
active.description: Cable wakeboard parks north of Bangkok run all day at a flat fee — no boat required, full circuit, and you'll fall off more times than you expect.
active.bonus: Ride the full circuit without falling off. It takes more attempts than it looks.

active.title: Cycle the Bang Kachao green lung loop
active.description: The 'green lung' opposite Klong Toei is a car-free peninsula of jungle, farms, and canals accessible by ferry — rent a bicycle and lose the city for a morning.
active.bonus: Find the botanical garden inside the loop. It's hard to find. Find it anyway.

active.title: Stand-Up Paddleboard on the Chao Phraya at Sunrise
active.description: Bangkok Kayak & SUP launches boards from the Yodpiman Riverside pier into the golden pre-traffic Chao Phraya for the most surreal active hour in the city.
active.bonus: Paddle close enough to a passing rice barge to wave at the crew — and get a wave back.

active.title: Pad Yak Kickboxing Class at Evolve MMA, Sukhumvit
active.description: Train alongside professional Muay Thai fighters at one of Asia's top gyms for a session that will leave your shins humming and your confidence high.
active.bonus: Ask your pad holder to call the combinations in Thai only — no English — after round two.

active.title: Run Lumphini Park at Dawn
active.description: Bangkok's 142-acre green lung fills before 7am with runners, tai chi groups, and monitor lizards making Lumphini the city's most democratic public space.
active.bonus: Spot and photograph a monitor lizard before you finish your second lap.

active.title: Muay Thai Morning Training at Sor Vorapin Gym
active.description: One of Bangkok's oldest active training gyms near Rattanakosin has been running tourist sessions alongside professional fighters since the 1980s — 90 minutes of pads, bags, and clinch work that leaves you wrung out by 9am.
active.bonus: Finish every round. Don't tap out early — the trainers respect the ones who last.

active.title: Full-Day Muay Thai Camp Immersion at Fairtex
active.description: Fairtex's Bangkok training center runs a fighter's full-day schedule — conditioning at 6am, technical pad work mid-morning, a light Thai lunch with the team, and live sparring in the afternoon with resident fighters who don't go easy.
active.bonus: Stay for the second session even when your legs say no. The second session is the one that matters.
